blocks.text: Types of Vacant Land and Building Lots in Abbotsford

parts.t: Active vacant land listings in Abbotsford fall into three primary categories, each with different financing, servicing, and permitting rules: (1) serviced urban building lots in subdivisions on Eagle Mountain, McKee Peak, and infill pockets across Central Abbotsford and Clearbrook, where municipal water, sanitary sewer, storm sewer, and road frontage are already at the lot line; (2) rural residential acreage lots on Sumas Mountain (Straiton), Bradner, and Aberdeen, which typically require a drilled water well and an engineered Type 1 or Type 2 onsite septic system; and (3) vacant Agricultural Land Reserve (ALR) farmland in Matsqui Prairie, Sumas Prairie, Bradner, and Poplar.

Buyers evaluating infill or redevelopment land inside the urban containment boundary should check the property against the City of Abbotsford Official Community Plan (OCP) and specific neighbourhood plans—including the McKee Neighbourhood Plan, City Centre Plan, Historic Downtown Plan, and UDistrict Plan—to confirm permitted density, Development Cost Charges (DCCs), road dedication requirements, and tree-protection rules.

blocks.text: Financing, Servicing, and Geotechnical Checks on Abbotsford Land

parts.t: Unlike purchasing an existing house with a 5% to 20% down payment, Canadian banks and credit unions typically require a 35% to 50% down payment for raw or unserviced land, or a residential construction draw mortgage when buying a serviced building lot with approved building plans. Before removing subjects on any Abbotsford lot, verify servicing connection fees at City Hall (32315 South Fraser Way), check Steep Slope, Streamside Protection (RIPARIAN), and Floodplain Development Permit Area overlays on the City of Abbotsford webmap, and confirm whether GST applies to the land purchase price.

blocks.text: 7 Common Questions About Abbotsford Lots and Land

parts.t: Where can I find serviced residential building lots in Abbotsford?

Serviced single-family building lots most commonly come up in hillside subdivisions on Eagle Mountain and McKee Peak in Abbotsford East, or as newly subdivided infill lots in Central Abbotsford, Clearbrook, and Poplar.
How much down payment do I need to buy vacant land in Abbotsford?

Conventional Canadian lenders generally require 25% to 35% down for a fully serviced urban residential lot and 35% to 50% down for unserviced rural or agricultural land, unless paired with an approved residential construction draw mortgage.
Is GST applicable on vacant lots and land in Abbotsford?

Most newly subdivided builder lots, developer parcels, and commercial/agricultural land listings are subject to 5% GST, whereas certain personal-use resales of vacant land by an individual may be GST-exempt. Always verify GST status in writing before offering.
What Development Permit Areas (DPAs) affect building lots in Abbotsford?

Key City of Abbotsford overlays include the Steep Slope Development Permit Area (on Eagle Mountain, McKee, and Sumas Mountain), the Streamside Protection DPA near creeks and ravines, the Wildfire Interface DPA, and the Floodplain DPA on Sumas and Matsqui prairies.
Can I build a house on vacant ALR land in Abbotsford?

Yes, generally one principal residence up to 500 square metres (5,382 sq ft) of total floor area is permitted on a vacant ALR parcel under ALC and City of Abbotsford A1/A2 zoning, provided siting, floodplain elevation, well, and septic requirements are met.
How do I check municipal water and sewer connections for an Abbotsford lot?

You can view water, sanitary sewer, and storm main locations directly on the City of Abbotsford GIS webmap (abbotsford.ca/city-services/maps) and confirm exact latecomer charges or connection fees with the City Engineering department.
